scope_plain: Every Oregon voter. Most votes wins; no runoff. Oregon allows fusion nominations, so two candidates show two party labels on the ballot: Kotek as 'Democrat, Working Families' and Drazan as 'Republican, Libertarian.' Names appear in this year's random ballot order: Smith, Kotek, Drazan.
office_explainer: Runs the state government, signs or vetoes laws, proposes the budget, and appoints agency heads and judges.
why_it_matters: Four-year term. The governor sets the state's direction on housing and homelessness, the behavioral health system, schools, wildfire, and transportation funding, and fills vacancies on Oregon courts.

candidates.name: Brett Smith
candidates.background: Inventor, welder, fabricator and small business owner; no prior government experience. Ran for Congress in Oregon's 5th District in 2024 as an Independent Party candidate and finished third with 4.7%.

own_words.text: Frames his run as 'The Protest Vote': "To Independents, third-party and unaffiliated. It's you that will make or break this race."
Pledges "a full audit of our systems and tax code by independent contractors," "healthcare for all," and "a permanent moratorium on data centers."

candidates.name: Tina Kotek
candidates.background: Governor since January 2023. Before that, Oregon House Speaker and state representative; worked at Oregon Food Bank and Children First. Won the May 2026 Democratic primary with 86%.

own_words.text: "Fighting back against the rising cost of housing," by "cutting red tape to build more affordable homes." Says Oregon has outpaced the nation in new housing production.
"Supports moratoriums on new data centers," and is "charting a path to statewide universal preschool" with "more learning time - not shorter school years."
Says she declared a housing emergency and increased shelter and treatment beds, and "will continue the fight to reduce homelessness."

candidates.name: Christine Drazan
candidates.background: State senator from Canby; former state representative and House Republican Leader. The 2022 Republican nominee for governor. Won the May 2026 Republican primary with 41%; the Libertarian Party cross-nominated her in July.

own_words.text: "On day one, Christine will order state agencies to repeal rules, fees and mandates driving up the cost of housing, energy, food, transportation, childcare and healthcare."
The Drazan Plan: "Break the cycle of homelessness and addiction," "Restore graduation requirements and fix our schools," and "Audit spending and deliver results."
"Our problems are not partisan problems; they are leadership problems."

scope_plain: Every Oregon voter. Most votes wins; no runoff. Fusion labels on the ballot: Merkley as 'Democrat, Working Families,' Henry as 'Progressive, Pacific Green.' Ballot order this year: Smith, Merkley, Dye, Henry.
office_explainer: One of Oregon's two senators in Washington. Votes on federal laws, budgets, treaties and judges.
why_it_matters: Six-year term. Senators confirm federal judges and cabinet members and set national policy on taxes, health care, immigration and public lands, which cover more than half of Oregon.

candidates.name: David Brock Smith
candidates.background: State senator and Senate deputy Republican leader from Port Orford in southwest Oregon; former state representative and Curry County commissioner; small business owner. Won the May 2026 Republican primary over several opponents.

own_words.text: "Making Oregon Affordable": says he "fought Kotek's-Gas-Tax, stopped new tax-hikes," and will keep working to eliminate fraud and cut unnecessary spending.
"Ending the Homelessness Crisis: We need drug and mental health treatment that works!" Wants to "bring an end to permanent street camping."
Wants data centers held accountable so their costs aren't "shifted onto Oregon households."

candidates.name: Jeff Merkley
candidates.background: U.S. senator since 2009, seeking a fourth term. Former Oregon House Speaker and state representative; worked at Habitat for Humanity and as a national security analyst. Grew up in and still lives in east Portland.

own_words.text: His stated vision: "Families thrive, and the rich pay their fair share."
"Save our elections: Stop gerrymandering. Require paper ballots. End secret campaign funding. Expand vote-by-mail."
On housing and costs: "Ban hedge funds from buying single-family homes" and "stop drug companies from price gouging."

candidates.name: Gary Lyndon Dye
candidates.background: Portland-born engineering consultant with past work in natural gas measurement and oil refining. Ran for U.S. Senate as a Libertarian in 2020, for Metro Council President in 2022, and in the 2024 Republican primary for the 3rd Congressional District. Chose not to submit a Voters' Pamphlet statement.

own_words.text: No 2026 statement. The state pamphlet marks him as a candidate who 'chose not to submit a voters' pamphlet statement.'
From an earlier run: "We need to rid ourselves of career politicians."

candidates.name: Chris Henry
candidates.background: Long-haul truck driver and former UAW aircraft mechanic; union shop steward and organizer. Has run before as a Progressive: U.S. Senate 2022 (1.9%), State Treasurer 2020 (4.4%), Portland City Council District 4 in 2024.

own_words.text: "Cut massive U.S. military" spending and "end pointless wars."
"Medicare for All," and "triple the $7.25/hour minimum wage, same since 2009."
Wants a federal "Shaky Day Fund" to prepare Oregon for the Cascadia earthquake, and says "no special interests are funding my campaign."
